raw_evidence_cards.document_title: EvolveGCN: Evolving Graph Convolutional Networks for Dynamic Graphs
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: EvolveGCN adapts the graph convolutional network (GCN) along the temporal dimension by using an RNN to evolve the GCN parameters, capturing the dynamism of graph sequences without relying on node embeddings.
overlaps: Models dynamic graphs as a sequence of graph snapshots over time (technical feature 1)
Uses a recurrent neural network to learn temporal dynamics of graph sequences (technical feature 4)
Addresses the GNN+RNN combination where GNNs act as feature extractors and RNNs perform sequence learning
differences: Does not use graph summarization to compress the original graph into a fixed-size new graph
Does not use a graph autoencoder with reconstruction error to train node representations
Uses the RNN to evolve GCN network parameters rather than feeding single-time-step graph representations into an RNN
Does not address the issue of GNN outputs not being directly feedable into RNN via graph compression

sources.title: EvolveGCN: Evolving Graph Convolutional Networks for Dynamic Graphs
sources.quote: The proposed approach captures the dynamism of the graph sequence through using an RNN to evolve the GCN parameters.

sources.title: EvolveGCN: Evolving Graph Convolutional Networks for Dynamic Graphs
sources.quote: These methods use GNNs as a feature extractor and RNNs for sequence learning from the extracted features (node embeddings).

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: DTFormer: A Transformer-Based Method for Discrete-Time Dynamic Graph Representation Learning
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: DTFormer introduces a Transformer-based representation learning method for Discrete-Time Dynamic Graphs (DTDGs), pivoting from the traditional GNN+RNN framework to address its limitations including scaling to large graph sizes.
overlaps: Models dynamic graphs as successive graph snapshots (technical feature 1)
Addresses the GNN+RNN architecture and its scaling limitations for large graphs (motivation of technical feature 2)
Processes static snapshots with graph neural networks and integrates representations over time
differences: Uses a Transformer-based architecture instead of graph summarization + graph autoencoder + RNN
Does not compress the original graph into a fixed-size new graph via graph summarization
Does not use a graph autoencoder with reconstruction error for node representation training
Does not feed single-time-step graph representations into an RNN for temporal learning

sources.title: DTFormer: A Transformer-Based Method for Discrete-Time Dynamic Graph Representation Learning
sources.quote: GNN+RNN architectures also grapple with scaling to large graph sizes and long sequences.

sources.title: DTFormer: A Transformer-Based Method for Discrete-Time Dynamic Graph Representation Learning
sources.quote: static graph neural networks, such as GNNs (17) and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) (18), are used to process static snapshots of the graph to capture topological relationships.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: ADWISE: Adaptive Window-based Streaming Edge Partitioning for High-Speed Graph Processing
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: ADWISE proposes a window-based streaming edge partitioning algorithm that assigns individual graph edges to partitions in a streaming manner, dynamically adapting window size to balance partitioning latency and partitioning quality for large graphs.
overlaps: Edge-based streaming graph partitioning: assigns individual graph edges to partitions in a streaming manner
Targets very large graphs and distributed graph processing
Aims to reduce partitioning/processing latency and improve partitioning quality
differences: ADWISE uses a window-based selection strategy (choosing the best edge from a set) rather than edge-segmentation with Count-Min Sketch
No Count-Min Sketch probabilistic data structure is used for storing node degree information
No min-heap is used to maintain high-frequency node information
Does not describe constant-time (O(1)) query results or subgraph-ID generation based on degree estimation

sources.title: ADWISE: Adaptive Window-based Streaming Edge Partitioning for High-Speed Graph Processing
sources.quote: Existing graph partitioning algorithms minimize partitioning latency by assigning individual graph edges to partitions in a streaming manner --- at the cost of reduced partitioning quality.

raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: WStream is a window-based streaming graph partitioning algorithm (edge-cut) that partitions large graph data in a one-pass manner while keeping load balanced across partitions and minimizing communication.
overlaps: Streaming graph partitioning for large-scale graph data
Load balancing across partitions
One-pass (streaming) processing of graph data
differences: WStream is a vertex-assignment (edge-cut) partitioning algorithm that distributes vertices, not edge-segmentation-based subgraph-ID generation
No Count-Min Sketch probabilistic data structure for degree storage
No min-heap for high-frequency node maintenance
Does not describe constant-time query results or degree-based subgraph assignment

sources.title: Window-based Streaming Graph Partitioning Algorithm
sources.quote: Our results suggest that the WStream algorithm is able to partition large graph data efficiently while keeping the load balanced across different partitions, and communication to a minimum.
